newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MMS proposes central Gulf oil, gas lease sale.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MMS proposes central Gulf oil, gas lease sale.

text.p: The U.S. Minerals Management Service on Friday proposed to offer 5,040 blocks covering 27 million acres in a new oil and natural gas lease sale in the central Gulf of Mexico.
The outer continental shelf blocks for proposed lease sale 166, scheduled for March 1997, are in water depths of three to more than 3,200 meters off Louisiana, Mississippi and Alabama.
Under a law passed this year, successful bids on blocks in water 200 meters or deeper would be eligible for royalty relief.
The tax break helped attract a record high number of bids and resulted in a record number of blocks leased in a Central Gulf sale this year, MMS said.

Under a final rule issued October 30, tracts in water 400 to 800 meters deep will be leased for eight year terms, and tracts in water deeper than 800 meters will have an initial lease term of 10 years.
In its notice of proposed sale, MMS sought comment on a request by the state of Alabama that unleased blocks south and within 15 miles of Baldwin County not be offered in the sale.
